chart_values:
# Chart values for the benchmark deployment. Everything here is either the
# hardware budget or a value the benchmark needs to observe; the service's own
# defaults are left alone, because a benchmark of a tuned-for-the-benchmark
# configuration measures the tuning.
image:
  registry: tapbench
  tag: bench
  pullPolicy: Never

tapApi:
  replicas: 1
  # The load generator runs on the host, so the URLs the service hands out
  # (UWS job locations, result links) have to be reachable from there. Left at
  # the in-cluster default, every async job would return a location pointing at
  # a Service name the generator cannot resolve, and the KEDA scenarios would
  # measure DNS failures.
  baseUrl: "http://127.0.0.1:30080/tap"
  # One worker per pod. The replica count is the variable under test, and a
  # pod that also scales internally would make "throughput per replica" mean
  # two different things at once.
  workers: 1
  resources:
    requests: {cpu: 1, memory: 512Mi}
    limits: {cpu: 2, memory: 1Gi}

tapExecutor:
  replicas: 1
  # CPU limit 1, not 2: the executor is a single thread, and under sustained
  # load it pins at ~0.96 cores with zero throttling — a 2-core limit is one
  # core it can never use, and headroom in the numbers that does not exist.
  # Per-pod throughput (~2 jobs/s) is set by the single thread, not by CPU;
  # replicas are the executor's scaling axis.
  resources:
    requests: {cpu: 500m, memory: 512Mi}
    limits: {cpu: 1, memory: 1Gi}

# Both autoscalers are configured here and switched on per scenario, so the
# KEDA runs use the repository's real ScaledObject rather than one written for
# the benchmark.
horizontalAutoscaling:
  tapApi:
    enabled: false
    minReplicas: 1
    maxReplicas: 8
    targetCPUUtilizationPercentage: 70
  tapExecutor:
    enabled: false
    scaler: keda
    minReplicas: 1
    maxReplicas: 8
    queuedJobsPerReplica: 10
    prometheusAddress: http://prometheus.benchmon.svc:9090
    pollingIntervalSeconds: 5

verticalAutoscaling:
  enabled: false

metrics:
  scrapeAnnotations: true

# The benchmark's own Prometheus scrapes the pods (manifests/monitoring.yaml);
# the chart's bundled one would be a second scraper on the same endpoints.
prometheus:
  enabled: false

config:
  # 8 per process against an 8-CPU server: the pool is the concurrency limit
  # under test, so it is stated rather than left at whatever the default is.
  # Unchanged when the server's cores doubled, because moving the pool and the
  # cores together would leave nothing to attribute a change to.
  dbPoolMin: 1
  dbPoolMax: 8
  dbPoolTimeoutSeconds: 5
  syncTimeoutSeconds: 60
  asyncExecDurationSeconds: 600
  hardMaxrec: 1000000
  defaultMaxrec: 10000
  logLevel: WARNING
  executorMetricsPort: 9100

results:
  size: 5Gi

postgresql:
  enabled: true
  storage: 200Gi
  resources:
    requests: {cpu: 4, memory: 4Gi}
    limits: {cpu: 8, memory: 12Gi}
  tuning:
    # pg_stat_statements and I/O timing are requirements of the suite, not
    # tuning: without them there is no per-statement or per-relation I/O data
    # to attribute anything to.
    shared_preload_libraries: pg_stat_statements
    track_io_timing: "on"
    "pg_stat_statements.max": "10000"
    "pg_stat_statements.track": all
    # Sized for the 12 GiB limit: shared_buffers a quarter of it, the rest left
    # to the page cache, which is where a 45 GiB database lives or does not.
    shared_buffers: 3GB
    effective_cache_size: 8GB
    work_mem: 32MB
    maintenance_work_mem: 512MB
    max_connections: "200"
    max_wal_size: 4GB
    random_page_cost: "1.1"

cluster.postgres: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on x86_64-pc-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit
